_schema.name: short id used in results table
_schema.urls: map of transport → URL; keys: raw-quic, h3-wt
_schema.disabled: bool; if true, skip this relay entirely (default false)
_schema.disabled_suites: list of interop suite names to skip for this relay
_schema.xfail_suites: interop suites that run and report but never gate for this relay: a documented peer non-conformance the case correctly fails on. A list, or a map of suite → reason printed with the XFAIL
_schema.namespace: load_sim namespace for relay-pub-sub (default: aiomoqt), for relays that scope publishing by namespace
_schema.compat: list of WIRE tolerance keys passed to the tools as --compat (libquicr, lenient-extensions, ...); the tools reject unknown values
_schema.gating: list of draft numbers whose results gate CI (a FAIL fails the job). Absent/empty = non-gating: the relay still runs and reports, but its failures are XFAIL and never gate. Curate this to endpoints we hold ourselves to.

relays.name: moqx-main
relays.notes: openmoq moqx CI relay. Covers drafts 16/18 over both raw-QUIC and H3/WT (/moq-relay); moqx dropped d14.

relays.name: cloudflare-d14
relays.notes: CF d14 moq-rs: publisher must send PUB_NS + PUBLISH. It answers neither FETCH, joining FETCH included (cloudflare/moq-rs#57, #58), nor SUBSCRIBE_ANNOUNCES, so fetch, join and discovery are disabled.

relays.name: moxygen-fb
relays.notes: Upstream moxygen/mvfst reference relay, the conformant d16/d18 reference. d14 runs non-gating.

relays.name: moq-dev-anon
relays.notes: moq-dev-rs (moq-lite) anon endpoint. Refuses PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS as not supported, which relay-discovery reports.

relays.name: quicr-west

xfail_suites.relay-fetch: intermittent FIN mid-object on its FETCH stream, likely an Object Status, which FETCH objects do not carry

relays.notes: Cisco libquicr (server cert unacceptable → insecure). Serves d18 only: moqt-16 and moqt-20 are refused in TLS. Its WT endpoint (/relay) answers CONNECT with 404, so only raw QUIC is listed. compat=libquicr covers two non-spec behaviors, tolerated + annotated: (1) relay returns SUBSCRIBE_OK for a nonexistent track (deferred-delivery policy); (2) relay returns FETCH_ERROR code=0 (INTERNAL_ERROR) for a nonexistent-track FETCH — the fetch probe honors libquicr code=0 as a deliberate refusal (the relay answered structurally in ~85ms; it just uses a poor code), matching how the join probe already accepted its non-spec code=17. Without --compat the fetch probe still fails code=0 by default (0x0 is not a refusal).

relays.name: imquic
relays.notes: Meetecho imquic (C). d14 probes rejected (WT: "No WebTransport protocol offered"; QUIC close 376). publish-ns: a PUBLISHed track reaches only the first of several subscribers. Peer issues seen: namespaces come back display-escaped ('-' → '.2d'), and the d16/d18 FETCH_OK End Location can precede the FETCH's Start.

relays.name: nokia-d18
relays.notes: Nokia Research draft-18 relay (independent impl) on :8443; draft-22 is nokia-d22 on :4443.

relays.name: cf-d18-interop
relays.notes: Cloudflare moq-rs draft-18 interop relay; publisher sends PUB_NS + PUBLISH.

relays.name: nokia-d22

xfail_suites.relay-join: its fill fetch stream intermittently carries an Object Status, which FETCH-delivered objects do not (d22 §11.1.1)

relays.notes: Nokia Research draft-22 relay on :4443; draft-18 is nokia-d18 on :8443.

relays.name: stitcher-moq
relays.notes: Stitcher MoQ (moq-dev deployment), drafts 18/20/22. Publishing is scoped to moq-test/*. Refuses PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS and multi-group FETCH as not supported, and serves no fill.
